title: Stand-ins for the broken game classes that free the most ports, and super calls they answer
text: Ranked every broken game class on main's jar scoreboard (each update's per-mod missing lists, cloud-exposure 45102116472) by the ports it would free if every missing member of it were answered, counting a port only when every reference it still needs is a stand-in kind (calls, fields, gone classes, method references; not mixins, overrides or loader events) and is covered. Stand-ins written top-down from that ranking for the updates up to 1.21.4 and the members of later ones answered before the split with the newest-updates thread, each read from both releases' code and cited to the loaders' migration notes; classes covered by #196 or #197 skipped. The porter now lets a stand-in for an old instance method answer a mod's super call to it (the old method is gone from every class above the mod's; the stand-in is that old game code), except inside a body moved to a game method's new parameters, where the stand-in could call that body back.
finish: The ports the written stand-ins alone held back link on the updates they touch, no update loses a mod, and freed mods load in a real game
wrongIf: a freed mod fails in game on a stand-in, or a super call answered by a stand-in recurses or runs other code than the old game method
result: Ranking main's 87 per-update and per-jump held lists by class showed the reachable ceiling is lower than a blind count: of 4,740 held ports only 1,145 are held by stand-in kinds alone (calls, fields, gone classes), and the best 100 classes free 386 of them, mostly through classes another PR owns (#197's list constructors) or redesigns with no honest answer (1.21.6's shader colour and drawSpecial, 1.21 enchantments, 1.20 Material, whose route already goes to BlockState). Written: 1.20.5 item tag access over CUSTOM_DATA, hurtAndBreak, isEdible, tooltips, pings, profiles, map ids, the Ogg stream; 1.21 attribute modifiers by UUID; 1.21.4 AbstractWidget.clicked; 1.21.9 label drawing and ChatScreen; 1.21.11 permission levels, label drawing, item modifier sums; 26.3 double smoothstep, link screens from text, swinging; 1.19/1.19.3/1.19.4/1.20.3 small getters. The porter lets stand-ins answer super calls, which freed mods whose own stand-ins already existed (Mod Menu 1.21.4, Bountiful and Traveler's Backpack 1.18). Cloud scoreboard 45115435581 against main 517899422b: every update 6,605 -> 6,636 (+31), big updates 2,447 -> 2,478, newest game 22 -> 23, jumps +10 (Fabric 1.20.1 -> 26.3 6 -> 7), no update lower. In game (cloud-load 45115603013, 45115603268, 45115603297, 45115603124): 9 of 11 freed mods load; Necronomicon is a Forge jar NeoForge cannot construct, LambDynamicLights fails on its data pack in a 26.3 client. Left: super(...) calls to changed constructors, which stand-ins cannot answer (26.1 Tooltip, 1.20.3 lists, 1.17 renderers), and the rendering rewrites with no honest answer.
